title: Facility Lockdown Notice
speaker: Dr. Elias Voss
text:
EFFECTIVE IMMEDIATELY. Saltmere Annex is closed under clause 14 (containment). All staff out by 18:00. Leave samples in the cold vault. Leave logs where they are.

No incident report will be filed from this site. Questions go to me and to nobody else.

The lift to the crypt stays powered for the salvage crews. Everything else goes dark.

E. Voss

title: New Staff Orientation Card
text:
WELCOME TO SALTMERE ANNEX

B1: reception, patient ward, observation, labs, whiteboard bay.
B2: security wing, armory, coolant plant, cooling chamber, cold vault.

B2 is card-controlled. Your card is not a B2 card. Do not ask.

The crypt lift is the only way up to the island. It takes two minutes and it is loud. If you are claustrophobic, say so now, not at minute one.

title: Sign-In Sheet (last page)
text:
DATE / NAME / PURPOSE / OUT

14th / R. Imes / damp survey / 11:40
14th / R. Imes / damp survey / 16:02
22nd / salvage crew (3) / cable recovery / 19:15

--- sheet skips four months ---

3 days ago / O. QUINN / sample recovery, cold vault, B2 clearance issued / ----

No out time. The pen is still clipped to the board.

title: Intake Form: Subject 7
speaker: Dr. Ines Calder
text:
SUBJECT 7. Ezra Penhallow, 68. Fisherman, Saltmere. Referred by the island clinic.

Condition: terminal, four to seven weeks. Weight down 19 kg. Can no longer stand for a full minute.

Consent: given, witnessed, read back to him twice. He asked whether it would hurt. I said I did not know. He said that was honest.

Note for the file: he is not a volunteer of convenience. He is a dying man who was offered strength. I want that written down by someone who was in the room.

I. Calder

title: Ward Nurse's Page
speaker: R. Imes
text:
Day eleven with Subject 7.

He calls me girl, which I have decided not to mind. He talks about the boat he sold. He says the worst part of dying was not being able to carry his own gear down the slip.

Today he carried his own water jug to the bed. He laughed about it for a long time. Then he laughed for a bit too long.

Dr. V came down to watch him do it and wrote four lines and left. He did not say one word to Ezra. Not one.

title: Trial Footage, Reel 1: Intake
text:
Grainy monochrome, ward lighting, timecode 00:00:11.

An old man sits on the edge of a bed in a gown, elbows on his knees, breathing in a way that takes effort. A gloved hand swabs his arm.

EZRA: "Will it be quick, either way?"
CALDER (off camera): "We don't know."
EZRA: "Then put it in before I think about it."

The injection goes in. He watches it go in. The reel ends on him looking at the ceiling, counting under his breath.

title: Trial Footage, Reel 2: Day Fourteen
text:
Timecode 00:00:03. The same man, standing, no gown now, a vest and trousers that no longer fit.

He lifts a crate of ballast weights that two staff carried in together. He sets it down gently, which is somehow worse.

VOSS (off camera): "Again."

He lifts it again. His forearms are wrong, corded past what skin should hold. At 00:01:48 his head turns to the camera and stays turned for nine seconds without blinking.

VOSS (off camera, quiet): "There. That's the body I wanted."

title: Trial Footage, Reel 3: Day Fifteen, 04:20
text:
Night lighting. The camera is knocked off level in the first second and films the rest at an angle.

Two staff in the frame. One is trying to talk to him by name. He takes her off her feet without seeming to decide to.

The reel runs forty more seconds. There is no fighting in it after the first eight.

At the end, a door opens. Shoes, not running. Voss steps into frame, looks at the floor, then at the thing standing over it, and speaks to the room.

VOSS: "Log it as a success with a complication. Seal the level. Nobody outside this building hears the word accident."

title: Handheld Recorder, Last Entry
speaker: Owen Quinn
text:
(breathing, water dripping)

Third day. Cold vault's fine, samples are fine, nothing down here is fine.

I got a B2 card off the chief's board. If anyone reviews this, I took it, it's mine, leave my record alone.

(pause)

Mara. If this ever gets to you. I called the port about the container and they logged it and did nothing, and then I called you instead, and that was me putting it on you. That wasn't fair. You didn't open anything. I did the work that filled it.

Stairwell's flooding and the lift's at the top. I'm going to sit on the landing a while.

title: Folded Note in a Coat Pocket
speaker: Owen Quinn
text:
M —

If I'm late, the tide's in the stair and I'm waiting it out. Don't come down. I mean it this time.

The container is VGR-7718. It is not medical supplies. Whoever signs for it at the port is in it up to the neck.

Tell them it was me who said so, not you. You've got a job and a radio and a town. I've got a badge they can take off me.

— O

title: Photograph, Creased in Four
text:
Two people on a slip in summer, squinting. A boy of about nineteen with his arm around his sister's shoulders, both holding one fish between them as if it were a trophy.

On the back, in biro: "you hooked it, I carried it. O."

title: Maintenance Snag List
speaker: R. Imes
text:
SNAG 41 — B2 bulkhead reader goes dead maybe twice a week. It is NOT the cards.

The conduit plug in the grey wall box left of the frame works itself loose when the bulkhead slams. Open the box, push the plug home until it clicks twice, then swipe. Works every time.

SNAG 42 — the reader beeps for a good ten seconds while it resets and it carries down the whole corridor. Stand somewhere you can see both ends before you do it.

title: V-7 Trial Log, Sheet 07
speaker: Dr. Ines Calder
text:
STRAIN RESPONSE, THERMAL. Ninth repeat, same result.

V-7 holds together at blood warmth and at steady cold. What breaks it is being moved between the two. Call it a cold-shock ladder.

THE LADDER, in order, no stage skipped:
1. Chill the volume to +4 C and HOLD 90 s.
2. Drop to -12 C and HOLD 30 s.
3. Return to +4 C and HOLD 60 s.
4. Purge.

Three stages up and down, then purge. Bonds fail in stage 2 and cannot re-form in stage 3. Skip a stage and it re-forms stronger, so do not improvise.

This is the shape any inhibitor has to be built around. Written here because Dr. Voss will not put it in the main file.

title: Re: Re: Subject 7 reclassification
speaker: Dr. Ines Calder
text:
Elias,

You are calling it a therapy in the funding file and a candidate in the lab file and those are two different words.

It took hold in him because he was dying. That is not a feature. That is the only door it can get through, and the moment somebody strong is bitten by somebody who got through that door, the door stops mattering.

I am keeping my own notes. I am not doing it to spite you. I am doing it because in eight months nobody will remember who said what in this corridor.

Ines

title: Lab Whiteboard (half wiped)
text:
Written large across the top and not wiped:

   TRIAL 07 / RUN 03 — THERMAL

Under it, a table in the same hand:

   STAGE | TEMP  | HOLD
     1   |  +4 C |  90 s
     2   | -12 C |  30 s
     3   |  +4 C |  60 s
     4   | PURGE |   -

In the corner, boxed and underlined twice:

   CHAMBER INTERLOCK WILL NOT RELEASE THE VAULT UNTIL ALL FOUR STAGES RUN IN ORDER.
   PURGE LAST. PURGE EARLY = RELIEF VENT = START AGAIN.

title: Sticky Note on the Board Frame
text:
To whoever keeps knocking:

I am not coming out to the corridor every time you forget the office code. It is on the board you are standing in front of.

Trial number, then run number. Two digits each, in that order. Four buttons. If you cannot read a board you should not be in my office.

— SEC CHIEF

title: Security Chief's Day Book
text:
Last page, written in three sittings.

Sealed the level like he asked. Counted them out, counted the doors, signed the sheet. Two did not come out and I signed the sheet anyway.

Kept the master key. It is mine until somebody senior enough comes down here to take it off me, which will be never.

Later: head's hot. Bit through my own lip in the night and did not wake up for it. Fuel pack's chafing where the plate sits.

Later: I can hear the pumps through the floor and the pumps are off.

title: Cold Store Clearance VGR-7718
text:
VIGOR BIOTECH — MOVEMENT CLEARANCE

Consignment: VGR-7718. Origin: Saltmere Annex cold store. Destination: Vigor Tower via Port Halvern Yard C.
Declared contents: medical supplies, refrigerated.
Actual contents, internal line: V-7 stock, live, 14 units.

Cleared for transit, authorised: E. VOSS, Research Director.

Port handling and police escort countersigned:

   W. HALE, Chief of Police, Marrow Bay

Handwritten under the signature: "No customs hold. No manifest copy to the harbour office."

title: Annex closure, final
speaker: Dr. Elias Voss
text:
To site security, copy to nobody.

The two staff we lost are recorded as a plant-room accident. That is the only version. If a family asks, they ask the company, not you.

Subject 7 remains on the level. He is not a disposal problem, he is data. Keep the ward doors shut and the power on the lift.

We move the programme to the tower. Eight months and a better room and this becomes the thing I said it was.

E.V.

title: Armory Board
text:
RACK CHECK — signed weekly, last signature eight months old.

1. Bolt rifle ............ PRESENT
2. Bolt rifle ............ SIGNED OUT, SEC CHIEF, not returned
3. Shot ................. transferred to Yard C escort
4. Flare pistol ......... transferred to harbour master, Saltmere

Rifle rounds: two boxes. Count them in and out. I will know.

title: Taped to the Stair Door, B2
speaker: R. Imes
text:
PUMPS ARE OFF. Lower level is holding about a metre and rising a hand's width a week.

Do not wade it in boots you care about and do not wade it alone.

And before anyone laughs at me again: something took the float switch off its chain. The chain is bitten. I have kept it in my locker.

title: Cooling Chamber Operating Card
text:
Laminated, chained to the valve gallery rail.

VALVE 1 — BRINE INTAKE. Floods the chamber and pulls it down to +4 C.
VALVE 2 — CRYO. Takes a flooded chamber to -12 C. Will not bite on a dry chamber.
VALVE 3 — PURGE. Dumps the chamber to the sump and ends the run.

GAUGE above the gallery shows chamber temperature. A green HOLD lamp lights when the stage temperature is reached and goes out when the hold time is served.

Work the valves one at a time. Serve every hold. If the sequence is wrong the relief vent blows live steam across the gallery and the run resets.

title: Cold Vault Carousel Card
speaker: Dr. Ines Calder
text:
CAROUSEL 2, POSITION 1 — "A". Inhibitor base, cold-set. Stable at vault temperature, stable in a hand for a few hours, dead if it warms past that.

A on its own does nothing at all. It is one third of a thing.

B (binder) and C (carrier) were never made here. They are at the tower, and so is the only machine that will put the three of them together, and that machine wants the thermal ladder from sheet 07 or it spits the batch out.

Whoever is reading this: take all three or take none.

title: Into the tunnel
speaker: MARA
text: You're under the island now. I can hear the rock in your mic.

title: Into the tunnel
speaker: LEON
text: There's a bulkhead ahead with a company serial on it. Your island has a basement.

title: Into the tunnel
speaker: MARA
text: Nobody ever said a word about anything under the lighthouse.

title: Into the tunnel
speaker: LEON
text: That's usually the point of a basement. Stay on this channel.

title: Reception
speaker: LEON
text: Reception, lights on half, closure notice on the desk. Signed by a Doctor Voss.

title: Reception
speaker: MARA
text: Is there a sign-in sheet? Tell me if there's a sign-in sheet.

title: Reception
speaker: LEON
text: There is. Why does that matter to you right now?

title: Reception
speaker: MARA
text: (a long pause, then a metal sound at her end) There's a lift in the church crypt. I'm in it.

title: Reception
speaker: LEON
text: Mara, go back up.

title: Reception
speaker: MARA
text: It only goes one way once it starts. Two minutes.

title: After the third reel
speaker: LEON
text: Found their trial footage. A man named Penhallow. He was dying and he said yes.

title: After the third reel
speaker: MARA
text: Ezra? He sold his boat to my neighbour. We thought he died in a hospice.

title: After the third reel
speaker: LEON
text: He didn't. And the man running it stood in the room afterwards and called it a success.

title: After the third reel
speaker: MARA
text: (static, her breathing) Lift's slowing. I'm nearly down.

title: The stairwell
speaker: LEON
text: Technician. Vigor jacket. He's got a B2 card in his hand.

title: The stairwell
speaker: MARA
text: Don't move him.

title: The stairwell
speaker: LEON
text: You know him.

title: The stairwell
speaker: MARA
text: Owen. He's my brother. He worked for them.

title: The stairwell
speaker: MARA
text: He called me three days ago. He said a container was coming through the port and nobody should open it.

title: The stairwell
speaker: LEON
text: And you had a radio.

title: The stairwell
speaker: MARA
text: I had the whole port on a radio. I said nothing, because saying it meant saying his name.

title: The stairwell
speaker: MARA
text: Two nights later they opened it anyway. So it didn't even buy him anything.

title: The stairwell
speaker: LEON
text: (after a moment) I've seen what one phone call to the right desk does. Usually nothing.

title: The stairwell
speaker: MARA
text: That's not absolution.

title: The stairwell
speaker: LEON
text: No. It's a fact. Take the photo out of his pocket, leave him the coat. We need the card.

title: Hint: B2 bulkhead
speaker: MARA
text: The card's good, I watched it light the panel orange. So it isn't the card.

title: Hint: B2 bulkhead
speaker: MARA
text: There's a snag list back in the labs that moans about this exact reader. Grey wall box, left of the frame.

title: Hint: B2 bulkhead
speaker: MARA
text: Open the box, push the loose plug in until it clicks twice, then swipe. And watch the corridor, the reset beeps for ages.

title: Hint: security office code
speaker: MARA
text: Four digits and a note from a man who thought he was being funny. It's on the board.

title: Hint: security office code
speaker: MARA
text: Read the top line of the whiteboard, not the table. Trial number, then run number.

title: Hint: security office code
speaker: MARA
text: Trial seven, run three. Two digits each. Zero seven, zero three.

title: Hint: cooling chamber
speaker: MARA
text: The vault's holding its own door shut. It wants the chamber run properly first.

title: Hint: cooling chamber
speaker: MARA
text: That log you copied down. Four stages, plus four, minus twelve, plus four, purge. The gauge is the board, the valves are the pen.

title: Hint: cooling chamber
speaker: MARA
text: Intake until the lamp dies, cryo until it dies, shut cryo and intake again until it dies, then purge. Purge last or the vent blows.

title: The thing in the wing
speaker: MARA
text: That one's wearing armour.

title: The thing in the wing
speaker: LEON
text: It was wearing it before. Body's grown into the plate.

title: The thing in the wing
speaker: LEON
text: Don't trade shots with it. Doors and corners.

title: Cold vault
speaker: LEON
text: Component A. Calder's writing says it's a third of a cure.

title: Cold vault
speaker: MARA
text: A third is more than this island's had all night.

title: Cold vault
speaker: LEON
text: The other two are in their tower in the city. With the machine that mixes them.

title: Cold vault
speaker: MARA
text: Then we're going to the city. Say it like it's a plan and I'll believe it.

title: Hint: the Warden
speaker: MARA
text: Pistol's doing nothing to that plate. Use the room.

title: Hint: the Warden
speaker: MARA
text: Yellow gas valves on the bay walls. Open one, get him standing in it, then drop the blast door on the bay.

title: Hint: the Warden
speaker: MARA
text: The blast strips his back plate. There's a fuel line under it. Shoot the line while it's bare, you've got about four seconds.

title: After the Warden
speaker: MARA
text: He had the keys to every door down here and he still couldn't leave.

title: After the Warden
speaker: LEON
text: He sealed two people in and signed the sheet. Then he stayed with it.

title: After the Warden
speaker: MARA
text: The far wall's down. There's salt air coming through it.

title: Sea cave
speaker: LEON
text: Maintenance raft. Oars, a bailing can, and about a foot of freeboard.

title: Sea cave
speaker: MARA
text: I row. You've got the gun and I've got twenty years of this water.

title: Sea cave
speaker: LEON
text: Then I'll call it. Left and right, loud, and you don't argue.

title: Sea cave
speaker: MARA
text: Mainland's that way. Four miles of nothing to hide behind.

title: Hint: the Undertow
speaker: MARA
text: I can't steer and watch. Call it or we're on the rocks.

title: Hint: the Undertow
speaker: MARA
text: It opens that eye before it swings. That's your window, not after.

title: Hint: the Undertow
speaker: MARA
text: If it's got hold of the raft, shoot the arm, not the eye. Free us first.

title: The mainland shore
speaker: MARA
text: Marrow Bay. Half those streets should be lit.

title: The mainland shore
speaker: LEON
text: Count the sirens instead. They stopped moving an hour ago.

title: The mainland shore
speaker: MARA
text: Who do we hand that clearance sheet to? Because one of the names on it runs the police.

title: The mainland shore
speaker: LEON
text: Then we start with him. Pull the raft up past the tide line, we're not coming back for it.
